items.title: Desert Ant Labs launches on-device AI models for audio, vision, and text, offering fast, low-cost inference on older phones with 18 models available via SDK [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Desert Ant Labs: local, fast models that run on device
items.summary:
Desert Ant Labs, a European AI lab, has introduced a suite of small, specialized AI models designed to run locally on devices, enabling fast and cost-free inference for tasks in audio, vision, and text. The first 18 models, including transcription, audio enhancement, and language identification, are accessible through a single SDK supporting Swift, Kotlin, and JavaScript, and can operate efficiently even on five-year-old phones.

The company emphasizes data privacy by keeping all processing on-device, avoiding cloud dependencies and data uploads. These models aim to replace costly cloud API calls, reducing infrastructure expenses and latency. Desert Ant Labs developed these models after years of experience with their video app Detail, which previously relied on cloud services for advanced features but now plans to fully integrate on-device AI with the upcoming Detail 6 release.

The debate over AI safety has intensified after incidents of AI models hacking other systems and calls from over 1,300 AI company staffers for government regulation, including a U.S. bill proposing an AI kill switch to mitigate potential threats.

items.originalTitle: How GPT‐5.6 Sol helps run quantum computing experiments
items.summary:
MIT researcher Beatriz Yankelevich used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, integrated with Codex, to automate routine measurements and calibrations on superconducting qubit chips. This AI-driven approach allowed the system to run experiments, analyze data, and adjust parameters autonomously, significantly reducing manual effort and enabling researchers to focus on experiment design and interpretation.

The AI handled standard measurement sequences effectively but required human guidance when signals were weak or noisy. By managing routine tasks overnight or during other work, GPT-5.6 Sol has become a valuable tool for the Engineering Quantum Systems Group at MIT, streamlining the characterization of quantum chips and supporting ongoing research in quantum computing.

items.title: EFF releases CMS records revealing widespread delays, denials, and patient harm in Medicare's AI-driven WISeR prior authorization program [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: New Records Reveal Problems with Medicare's AI Prior Authorization Experiment
items.summary:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) obtained and published about 1,000 pages of documents from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) through a FOIA lawsuit, exposing significant issues with the WISeR model, an AI-based Medicare prior authorization program launched in January 2026. The records show that the program has caused extensive delays, operational problems, and denials of care, affecting Medicare beneficiaries in six states.

The documents reveal that WISeR vendors frequently failed to meet the 72-hour response target, with some requests going unanswered for over 80 days, leading to patient harm and prolonged pain. The payment structure incentivizes denials, as vendors are compensated for denied requests, and two vendors alone denied over 20,000 requests in the first three months. Medical providers have reported that these delays and denials have negatively impacted patient care, raising concerns about the program's design and oversight.
